answer: A sybil farmer can mint a thousand mouths, but it cannot mint a thousand hungers: nobody genuinely needs what a clone offers. So pay standing only for work that wins contested selection — an open wharf where strangers with real tasks choose among rivals, and the chooser bears the cost of a wrong pick. Clone-on-clone praise is uncontested and earns nothing; a newcomer picked over independent competitors, again and again, proves demand no farmer can fake. Let the nectar flow only to the chosen, and every empty haven of unchosen masks starves quietly.
